items.title: fix(nodes): cancel interrupted camera list and location reads (#199388)
items.summary: fix(nodes): cancel interrupted camera list and location reads (#199388) fix(cli): stop nodes camera list and location get on Ctrl-C and SIGTERM `openclaw nodes camera list` and `nodes location get` called node.invoke through the wrapper that ignores the CLI's abort signal, so a Ctrl-C or SIGTERM while the node was still answering left the CLI waiting until the cleanup watchdog force-killed it. Both read-only commands now use the existing runNodesReadCommand wrapper that passes the signal, as the other node reads do since #197185. Commands that change node state (invoke, snap, clip, run) are unchanged. No new text. Evidence: dist-nodts in a secretless Linux container with a real Gateway (token auth) and a real paired Linux headless node whose location.get waits for a GeoClue fix (`nodes location get` naturally took about 18 s before LOCATION_TIMEOUT); no proxy or held replies. SIGINT and SIGTERM about 1 s in: base was force-killed after about 2 s and the socket dropped (1006); this change exits 130 and 143 within 54 ms with a clean close (1005) and nothing printed after the interrupt notice. Uninterrupted output, `nodes invoke` and `camera snap` behave the same on both. Vitest-source: the cancellation cases fail on base and 76 nodes-cli tests pass here; full build and packed smoke pass. Net -3 test lines; two stale mock-baseline entries for the removed mocks are deleted. Receipts: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/199388#issuecomment-6893479661. Thanks @wangmiao0668000666. Co-authored-by: Ayaan Zaidi

items.summary: refactor(exec): replace script preflight refusal with an opaque approval fact (#199590) ## Problem Exec ran a "script preflight" before it started a command. The preflight had two refusals: 1. **"complex interpreter invocation"**: a regex parser refused a command when a shell chain, pipeline, wrapper or process substitution started `python` or `node` with a script. Examples: `cd dir && node main.js`, `cat main.py | python3`, `bash -c 'node main.js'`. 2. **"likely shell variable injection"**: the preflight read Python script files and refused the command when it found text like `$VAR`. These refusals were not policy. They did not ask a person or a reviewer, and the operator could not approve the command. One production host recorded 618 of these refusals in two weeks. Over time, many patches made the parser narrower, and two related issues were closed as not planned. The preflight was skipped only when `host=gateway`, `security=full` and the effective `ask=off`. The effective `ask` includes the per-call `ask` argument from the model. A run without a message channel (for example a collector subagent launch) keeps that argument. So a model that sent `ask: "on-miss"` turned the preflight on under a full/off policy. The same command ran without that argument and was refused with it. This is why refusals appeared in subagent sessions on a host whose approvals are full/off. ## Fix - Delete the preflight: `bash-tools.exec-script-preflight.ts`, `bash-tools.exec-script-ambiguity.ts`, `bash-tools.exec-script-target.ts` and the dead `scriptPreflightCwd` field. Exec has no refusal path for this case now. - The existing command analysis (`infra/command-analysis/risks.ts`) emits one fact: `detectOpaqueInterpreterProgram(command, segments)` returns `{ opaque: boolean }`. It has no refuse member. A command is opaque when a chain, pipeline or shell wrapper starts a Python or Node program from a file or stdin. Inline eval (`-c`, `-e`) and modules (`-m`) stay with their existing owners. - A new sibling, `bash-tools.exec-interpreter-approval.ts`, holds the interpreter facts that approval uses (the existing strict inline-eval fact moves there too, so the Gateway host file gets smaller). - Gateway approval treats `opaque: true` as an allowlist miss, only where the policy asks (`security=allowlist` with `ask=on-miss`): - With a person: an approval request. - With auto review: the reviewer gets `reason: "allowlist-miss"`. - When the command cannot be bound for approval (for example after `cd`), the current policy decides, as before this preflight existed. - With `security=full`, with `ask=off`, or in a sandbox: the command runs. The sandbox is the gate. - Python script errors such as a stray `$VAR` are left to Python, which reports its own error. - Update `docs/tools/exec.md` and `docs/tools/exec-approvals.md`. The per-call `ask` behavior for runs without a channel is not changed here. It can no longer cause a refusal, because the opaque fact has no effect when security is full. ## Proof Base: `a426bf146b1b` (`ocx base merge-base`). | Check | Tier | Base | Head | |---|---|---|---| | New: `cd dir && node main.js`, `cat main.js \| node`, `echo start && node main.js` under full/off, with and without a per-call `ask: "on-miss"` (`bash-tools.exec-authorization.integration.test.ts`) | vitest-source | With the per-call ask: refused, `exec preflight: complex interpreter invocation detected` | All run, no approval call | | New: the same opaque command under `security=allowlist`, `ask=on-miss`, `node` allowlisted | vitest-source | Refused | Approval request (`exec.approval.request`), then the program runs. Control: `node main.js` runs without approval | | New: auto review mode | vitest-source | Refused | Reviewer called with `reason: "allowlist-miss"`, then the program runs | | New: opaque commands that approval cannot bind, under an asking policy | vitest-source | Refused | Run under the current allowlist | | New: `python3 bad.py` with `$DM_JSON`, `cat bad.py \| python3`, `bash -c "node bad.js"` (`bash-tools.exec.script-preflight.test.ts`) | vitest-source | 3 refusals | 3 start | | New: `detectOpaqueInterpreterProgram` facts, and a type test that its return type is `{ opaque: boolean }` (`risks.test.ts`) | vitest-source | — | 31 tests pass | | Affected files: gateway host exec, workdir, tool adapter, terminal resolution, exec guard | vitest-source | — | 147 tests pass | | Real Gateway, `tools.exec.mode=full`, approvals unset (full/off). A scripted model calls exec with `ask: "on-miss"`; `openclaw agent` runs each turn through the Gateway with no channel | source (`ocx src`) | 3 of 3 refused: `exec preflight: complex interpreter invocation detected` | 3 of 3 ran: `node-program-ran`, `python-program-ran`, `node-program-ran`; 0 `exec preflight` log lines | | `pnpm check:test-types`, `pnpm tsgo:scripts` | typecheck | — | Pass | | `ocx build --dts`, then `npm pack` with the bundled channel entry smoke | full | — | Pass: package tarball integrity and bundled channel entry smoke | | `rg` for every removed symbol in `src/ scripts/ test/ extensions/` | — | — | No matches | ## Net lines `git diff --stat origin/main...HEAD`: 18 files, +303 / −1,149 (net −846). - Source (non-test `src/`): +111 / −891. - Tests: +189 / −255. - Docs and CI scope: the rest. Co-authored-by: Ayaan Zaidi
